title: Timelike completeness as an obstruction to C0-extensions
theorem_location: PDF pages 1-2; statement begins at the foot of page 1 and continues at the top of page 2
copyright_boundary: Two load-bearing fragments totaling 23 whitespace-delimited words are retained; all other content is a formal transcription or paraphrase.
hypotheses_fragment: Let (M,g) be a smooth (at least C2) time-oriented globally hyperbolic Lorentzian manifold.
endpoint_fragment: that has an end point on the boundary of M.
formal_theorem_transcription: smooth at least C2 + time-oriented + globally hyperbolic + admits a C0 extension => there exists a timelike geodesic with an endpoint on the extension boundary
scope_paraphrase: The cited Theorem 2 is orientation-neutral: for a smooth at least C2 time-oriented globally hyperbolic Lorentzian manifold, any C0 extension supplies a boundary-ending timelike geodesic. G324 derives the direction rather than importing a separate time-dual theorem: future timelike completeness excludes a future endpoint, so the supplied endpoint must be past-directed.
not_imported: past C0 inextendibility of the G323 metric
